standard.title: Analyse needs, develop design brief, select materials
standard.description: analyse needs or opportunities for designing; develop design briefs; and investigate, analyse and select materials, systems, components, tools and equipment to create designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can analyse needs or opportunities for designing, and investigate and select materials, systems, components, tools and equipment (AC9TDE8P01). They can develop basic design briefs. They have not yet developed design briefs independently that incorporate universal design or Safety by Design principles, nor analysed intellectual property rights in design contexts, nor interviewed community members to identify design needs.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students independently analyse needs or opportunities for designing; develop design briefs that incorporate user needs and ethical considerations; and investigate, analyse and select materials, systems, components, tools and equipment for designed solutions.

nodes.label: Analysing needs and design opportunities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse a need or opportunity for designing, including considering the needs of diverse users and communities.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify a genuine need or design opportunity from a given scenario; describe at least two user needs that a designed solution should address.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse a need or opportunity by investigating users, context and constraints; identify how different users (including diverse or community groups) have different needs; consider how sustainability, accessibility and Safety by Design principles shape what the designed solution must achieve.
wider: Analyse First Nations Australians' traditional grains (e.g. acacia) for their commercial and nutritional potential — develop a design opportunity statement that responds to this as a design brief starting point
Interview community members about accessibility requirements to identify an unmet need — document what the interviews revealed that desk research would not have found
Analyse new products designed to address sustainability issues (e.g. pool sanitisation, UV disinfection, disposable alternatives) — evaluate how well each responds to the identified need

response_modes.reason: Need analysis looks different for different user groups and contexts — a community accessibility need is identified differently from a sustainability opportunity or a commercial product gap. Multiple contexts build analytical flexibility in need identification.

success_criteria: Identifies a specific need grounded in user or context analysis — not just a product category
Describes at least two distinct user needs that the designed solution must address
nodes.hinge_reason: Shallow needs analysis produces a design brief at N2 that does not capture real user and sustainability requirements — a brief built on assumed needs drives design criteria and material selection at N3 that cannot be validated against actual stakeholder needs.

nodes.label: Developing a design brief
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can independently develop a design brief that defines the problem, identifies user needs, and establishes the scope and constraints of a designed solution.
nodes.minimum_width: Write a design brief that names the problem, identifies at least two user needs, and states at least one constraint or scope boundary.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a design brief independently that incorporates: a clear problem definition, identified user needs (including diverse users), sustainability and ethical considerations, universal design or Safety by Design principles where relevant, and scope and constraints that define what the solution will and will not address.
wider: Develop a design brief for a community need by iterating through consultation with community members — document how the brief changed through consultation
Develop a design brief that explicitly addresses Indigenous cultural and intellectual property rights — explain what considerations this adds to the brief that a standard brief would not include
Compare a brief developed from desk research alone with one developed through user interviews — analyse what the interviews added and why it matters

response_modes.reason: A design brief is a reasoning document — students who write briefs by filling in a template without connecting user needs to constraints to scope produce briefs that don't actually define the problem. The reasoning chain (who is this for? → what do they need? → what constrains the solution? → what is in/out of scope?) is what makes a brief useful.

success_criteria: Brief names a specific problem (not just a domain or product type)
At least two user needs are stated and connected to the problem
At least one constraint or scope boundary is explicit
nodes.hinge_reason: A design brief without specific constraints and assessable criteria makes N3 material and technology selection arbitrary — students cannot justify selections against criteria that don't exist, and the entire design rationale collapses.

nodes.label: Investigating, analysing and selecting materials, systems, components, tools and equipment
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate, analyse and select appropriate materials, systems, components, tools and equipment for a design project with justification.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate at least two options for a key material, component or tool; analyse each against at least one criterion from the design brief; select one and justify the choice.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate a range of materials, systems, components, tools and equipment relevant to the design project; analyse each against criteria from the design brief (including sustainability, safety, cost, performance); select and justify choices; examine the compressive and tensile properties of structural materials where relevant.
wider: Investigate materials that raise intellectual property considerations — including Indigenous cultural and intellectual property rights — and explain how these must be addressed in the design process
Research a specialist material (e.g. bioplastic, composite) and evaluate whether it is appropriate for the design project given its properties, availability, cost and sustainability
Justify selections that prioritise sustainability over conventional choices — explain what you would accept as a trade-off and what you would not
success_criteria: At least two options are investigated for a key material or component
Selection is justified with reference to at least one criterion from the design brief
